=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:N/A | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The script mode changed from 100755 to 100644, removing the executable bit.
  WHY: Two reviewers reported the permission regression on this script; they disagreed on runtime impact, but both treated it as an unintended mode change.
- scripts/serena_stats_emit.py:N/A | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The script mode changed from 100755 to 100644, removing the executable bit.
  WHY: Two reviewers reported the permission regression on this script; they disagreed on runtime impact, but both treated it as an unintended mode change.
- scripts/setup_serena.sh:N/A | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The script mode changed from 100755 to 100644, removing the executable bit.
  WHY: Reviewers disagreed on impact: one said the executable bit is irrelevant because callers use bash, while others said direct invocation would fail with Permission denied.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~105-146 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The snapshot step still scales with the number of active workflow runs and can add timeout or rate-limit pressure on busy repos.
  WHY: Some reviewers treated the refactor as the intended API fanout reduction, while others still called out the active-run pagination cost.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~136-173 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The associative-array key `${workflow}:${head_ref}` can collide if `head_ref` contains `:`.
  WHY: Reviewers disagreed on whether `:` is possible in a valid branch name; some called it a hardening risk, others rejected it as impossible.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~112-122 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: A run that moves from `queued` to `in_progress` between the two API calls can be counted twice, inflating the advisory skip count.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers confirmed the race, but also agreed it does not affect the binary dispatch guard because any count > 0 still skips.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/setup_serena.sh:N/A | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: pass-1 claims the shell script lost executable permission, breaking direct invocation as ./setup_serena.sh
  WHY: git ls-tree on commit d43d7d5 confirms the original mode was 100644, every caller invokes it as bash scripts/setup_serena.sh, and the executable bit is irrelevant.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:105-143 | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: pass-1 claims the snapshot paginates and transcodes every queued/in_progress run across the repo, risking hang or timeout under large queues
  WHY: the endpoint is workflow-scoped, only active runs for the two workflows are fetched, and the new code makes at most 4 API calls total regardless of candidate count.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~136, ~173 | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: pass-1 claims a branch named feature:alpha would produce a key collision causing undercount
  WHY: both population and lookup use the identical `${workflow}:${head_ref}` expression and bash associative arrays treat the whole string as an opaque key.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:112-115 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: pass-1 correctly identifies that the same workflow run can appear in both API responses if its status changes between the queued fetch and the in_progress fetch
  WHY: the count is only used for advisory logging and a binary active>0 guard, so double-counting only inflates the displayed count.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py, scripts/serena_stats_emit.py, scripts/setup_serena.sh:N/A | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The serena scripts lost executable permission.
  WHY: These files are not part of issue #2582 requirements and the current 0644 permissions are inert, but the mode changes are still scope creep from the original implementation.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~105-140 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The snapshot still iterates over all active runs.
  WHY: This is the intended optimization: the sweep now makes 2 API calls plus local lookups instead of N×2 per-PR calls.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~136, ~173 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The key format `${workflow}:${head_ref}` uses `:` as a separator between workflow name and head_ref.
  WHY: Branch names containing `:` could theoretically cause a collision, though this was assessed as a low-risk theoretical edge case.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:snapshot_active_review_runs function | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A run transitioning from queued to in_progress between the two API calls can be counted twice.
  WHY: The count is only used for advisory logging and the dispatch decision is binary, so double-counting does not affect correctness.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py, scripts/serena_stats_emit.py, scripts/setup_serena.sh:N/A | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The autofix editor changed file permissions from 100755 to 100644 on three script files that are NOT part of the PR scope.
  WHY: Removing executable permissions can break direct invocation, and the PR description explicitly said to stay inside files_touched.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~136, ~173 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The associative array key uses `:` as a delimiter between workflow name and head_ref.
  WHY: While rare, branch names can legally contain colons, which could cause a collision and duplicate dispatches.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~119-122 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A workflow run that transitions from queued to in_progress between the two API calls can be counted twice.
  WHY: This only affects the logged count value and not dispatch correctness, but it makes the AUTOFIX_SWEEP_SKIP log lines misleading.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
(No findings reported.)
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_1-fast ===
- scripts/setup_serena.sh:N/A | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Shell script stripped of executable bit.
  WHY: Direct invocation from workflows or setup scripts fails with Permission denied because shebangs are ignored without +x.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~105-140 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Snapshot paginates and transcodes every queued/in_progress run repo-wide per workflow, even if most are irrelevant to the sweeped PRs.
  WHY: The implementation scales with active runs and can timeout or hit rate limits on pagination despite the status filter.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~136, ~173 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Key separator : collides with Git branch names containing :.
  WHY: Branch feature:alpha undercounts or merges with workflow/head combinations, which can lead to duplicate dispatches if the count drops to zero erroneously.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~112-120 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A run transitioning queued→in_progress between fetches can be counted twice per branch.
  WHY: This inflates the logged count in AUTOFIX_SWEEP_SKIP, which misleads operators even though dispatch remains correct for any count greater than zero.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_1-fast ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:~114 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A run that transitions from queued to in_progress between the two gh api calls can be counted twice in the associative array value.
  WHY: The two independent API calls can both observe the same run, inflating the advisory AUTOFIX_SWEEP_SKIP count while leaving the > 0 dispatch-skip check correct.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===
